sentence: High cholesterol, also called hypercholesterolaemia, means there is too much cholesterol in the blood.
note: Textbook definition and naming; pages retrieved are titled high cholesterol and hypercholesterolaemia.

sentence: High cholesterol does not usually cause symptoms, so a blood test is the only way to find out whether someone has it.
note: NHS: high cholesterol does not usually cause symptoms; you can only find out from a blood test.

sentence: LDL and non-HDL cholesterol are often called the bad cholesterol, and Heart UK describes them as the current evidence-based targets for lowering cholesterol and reducing the risk of cardiovascular disease.
note: Heart UK excerpt: non-HDL and LDL cholesterol (commonly the bad cholesterol) are the evidence based targets for lowering cholesterol and reducing risk of CVD. Page URL is a Heart UK HDL page; the same site returned the causes page.

sentence: HDL cholesterol is the good type.
note: Heart UK search summary: HDL is the good fraction.

sentence: Over time, high cholesterol builds up fatty material in the arteries, which raises the risk of coronary heart disease, heart attack and stroke.
note: BHF: fatty material builds in the arteries, raising risk of coronary heart disease, heart attack and stroke; NHS says the same about blocked blood vessels (search summary, not page-attributed).

sentence: High cholesterol can cause problems with the heart and blood vessels, which are known as cardiovascular disease.
note: Search summary quoted: having high cholesterol can cause problems with your heart and blood vessels (cardiovascular disease); the page was not named, so attributed to the NHS condition page with that caveat.

sentence: Familial hypercholesterolaemia significantly raises the risk of early heart disease.
note: BHF search summary: FH significantly raises risk of early heart disease.

sentence: Heart UK says lifestyle, genes and overall health can all have an effect on cholesterol, and these can add up.
note: Heart UK causes page: your lifestyle, your genes and your overall health can all have an effect, and these can all add up.

sentence: Lifestyle factors include alcohol, excess weight (especially around the middle), smoking, a diet high in saturated fat and low physical activity.
note: Heart UK lists alcohol, excess weight especially around the middle, smoking, unhealthy diet high in saturated fat, low physical activity.

sentence: The British Heart Foundation says that cholesterol in foods such as eggs and shellfish has only a minimal effect for most people, while saturated fat matters more.
note: BHF search summary: dietary cholesterol in eggs and shellfish has minimal effect for most people; saturated fat matters more.

sentence: High cholesterol can run in families.
note: NHS: it can run in families (search summary).

sentence: Familial hypercholesterolaemia is an inherited condition that causes very high LDL cholesterol from birth and lasts a lifetime.
note: BHF search summary: FH causes very high LDL from birth and lasts a lifetime; NHS England calls it inherited.

sentence: Other conditions, such as diabetes or thyroid disease, can affect cholesterol, so doctors rule them out first when familial hypercholesterolaemia is suspected.
note: Search summary: secondary causes such as diabetes or thyroid disease should be ruled out first; page not named, CG71 and the Genomics Education Programme page were both returned.

sentence: The NHS says people are more likely to develop high cholesterol if they are over 50, male, past the menopause, or of South Asian or sub-Saharan African origin.
note: NHS summary: more likely if over 50, male, post-menopausal, or of South Asian or sub-Saharan African origin.

sentence: A GP may suggest a cholesterol test for people who are over 40, overweight, or have a family history of high cholesterol or heart problems.
note: NHS summary: a GP may suggest a test if you're over 40, overweight, or have a family history of high cholesterol or heart problems.

sentence: Testing may also be offered as part of an NHS Health Check to some adults who do not already have cardiovascular disease.
note: Essex ICB (NHS) page: testing may be offered through an NHS Health Check for people aged 40 to 74 without existing cardiovascular disease; age band left out.

sentence: A test can also be done at some pharmacies, sometimes for a fee.
note: NHS summary: you can also get tested at a pharmacy, possibly for a fee.

sentence: A lipid profile blood test measures HDL cholesterol, non-HDL cholesterol, the cholesterol ratio, triglycerides and total cholesterol.
note: BHF: a lipid profile will measure HDL, non-HDL, cholesterol ratio, triglycerides, total cholesterol.

sentence: GPs also weigh age, blood pressure and other health conditions when estimating the chance of heart and circulation problems.
note: NHS cholesterol levels page summary: GPs also consider age, blood pressure and other conditions when estimating heart and circulation risk.

sentence: Familial hypercholesterolaemia can cause lumps on the knuckles, knees or the back of the ankle, or yellowish patches near the eyes, though these signs can be absent.
note: Search summaries: tendon lumps around knuckles, knees, Achilles tendon; yellowish patches near eyes; signs can be absent.

sentence: When familial hypercholesterolaemia is suspected, a clinician can use a scoring guide, and DNA evidence of a gene change can also support the diagnosis.
note: Search summary: a high result or signs prompt use of a scoring guide such as Simon Broome; diagnosis can rest on genetic evidence. Page not named.

sentence: NICE advises measuring LDL cholesterol twice in this situation because results naturally vary.
note: Search summary: NICE advises 2 measurements of LDL-C because biological and analytical variability occurs.

sentence: NICE recommends that people with familial hypercholesterolaemia are offered referral to a specialist, who confirms the diagnosis and starts testing of relatives.
note: Search summary: NICE recommends offering referral to a specialist for confirmation of diagnosis and initiation of cascade testing (testing relatives).

sentence: Treatment starts with lifestyle changes such as healthier eating and more activity, and some people also need medicine.
note: NHS: lifestyle changes come first, some also need medication; Essex ICB: for some people lifestyle changes alone are not enough.

sentence: Statins are the most common medicine for high cholesterol, usually taken as a daily tablet and often for the long term.
note: NHS: statins are the most common treatment, a daily tablet, usually long term.

sentence: Statins may be offered to people at higher risk of cardiovascular disease when healthy lifestyle changes have not helped, or to people who already have cardiovascular disease.
note: NHS statins page summary.

sentence: Most people can take statins, but they are not suitable for everyone, for example people with severe liver disease or who are pregnant.
note: NHS statins page summary: most people can take statins; not with severe liver disease, pregnancy or trying to get pregnant.

sentence: Atorvastatin is a statin used to lower cholesterol and to prevent heart disease, including heart attacks and strokes.
note: NHS atorvastatin: used to lower cholesterol and prevent heart disease including heart attacks and strokes.

sentence: Rosuvastatin is another statin, and the NHS says most adults can take it, though it is not suitable for everyone.
note: NHS rosuvastatin pages: most adults and children aged 6 and over can take it, but it isn't suitable for everyone.

sentence: NICE guidance on lipid modification names atorvastatin as the statin to offer for preventing cardiovascular disease, and describes rosuvastatin as an alternative in the same intensity group if a change is needed.
note: NICE NG238 summary: offer atorvastatin; changing to a different statin in the same intensity group (rosuvastatin if already receiving atorvastatin).

sentence: If statins do not suit a person or are not enough, the NHS lists other medicines such as ezetimibe, bempedoic acid and some injected medicines.
note: NHS: ezetimibe, bempedoic acid and injectables (alirocumab, evolocumab, inclisiran).

sentence: For familial hypercholesterolaemia, statins are the first treatment and care is usually overseen by specialist lipid clinics.
note: Search summary: statins first-line; treatment usually overseen by specialist lipid clinics.

sentence: Heart UK says that when lifestyle changes are agreed with a doctor, they are kept up for an agreed time before cholesterol is checked again.
note: Heart UK HDL page: lifestyle changes kept going for an agreed period before levels checked again.

sentence: Heart UK says regular aerobic exercise that raises the heart rate can improve LDL levels and lower triglycerides.
note: Heart UK low-HDL page: aerobic exercise improves LDL levels and lowers triglycerides.

sentence: Heart UK also says that losing weight can help raise HDL cholesterol.
note: Heart UK low-HDL page: weight loss helps raise HDL.

sentence: The NHS in Essex recommends improving diet, staying physically active and keeping to a healthy weight.
note: Essex ICB page.

sentence: The British Heart Foundation advises asking the GP for a cholesterol check, which is a simple blood test, and the doctor reads the result alongside other risk factors.
note: BHF summary: ask GP for a cholesterol check; doctor interprets alongside other risk factors.

sentence: Sudden chest pain or signs of a stroke need an emergency call to 999.
note: Standard emergency signposting; not returned by the cholesterol searches.
